settings.label: Domain
settings.meaning: The tenant's domain, such as acme.us.auth0.com, or its custom domain. Tokens are issued by https://<domain>/ and its keys are at https://<domain>/.well-known/jwks.json.
settings.whereToFind: Applications › [your application] › Settings › Domain. Auth0 keeps test and live apart by tenant: use another tenant for test, with its own domain and keys.

settings.label: Client ID
settings.meaning: The application users sign in to. Also the audience of its ID tokens.

settings.label: Client secret
settings.meaning: Authenticates the app's backend to Auth0 for the code exchange, refresh, sign-out and the other sign-in calls. Not needed only to verify tokens.
settings.whereToFind: Applications › [your application] › Settings › Client Secret (a Regular Web Application).

settings.label: API identifier
settings.meaning: The app's API in Auth0. When set, sign-in asks for access tokens for it and only tokens whose aud names it are accepted; when unset, the app's ID tokens (aud: the client ID) are.

settings.label: Management client ID
settings.meaning: A Machine to Machine application authorized for the Auth0 Management API, for reading, creating and deleting users. Needs read:users, create:users, update:users and delete:users.
settings.whereToFind: Applications › [your Machine to Machine application] › Settings › Client ID; authorize it for the Auth0 Management API under its APIs tab.

settings.label: Management client secret
settings.meaning: The Machine to Machine application's secret, exchanged for a Management API token (client_credentials) that lasts about a day.
settings.whereToFind: Applications › [your Machine to Machine application] › Settings › Client Secret.

settings.label: Tenant domain
settings.meaning: Only when AUTH0_DOMAIN is a custom domain: the tenant's own domain (acme.us.auth0.com). The Management API's audience always names it.
settings.whereToFind: Settings › Custom Domains shows the custom domain; the tenant's own domain is the one in any application's Settings before the custom domain was added.

settings.label: Database connection
settings.meaning: The database connection users are created in, sign in to with a password, and reset passwords for. Default Username-Password-Authentication.

settings.label: Event stream token
settings.meaning: Checks that a webhook came from the tenant's event stream. You choose it, and Auth0 sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every delivery.
settings.whereToFind: A long random string of your own (openssl rand -hex 32), entered as the Bearer Token when the webhook event stream is made: Event Streams › Create Event Stream › Webhook.

operations.name: tokens.exchangeCode
operations.purpose: Exchanges the authorization code from Universal Login, with its PKCE verifier, for tokens.

operations.name: tokens.refresh
operations.purpose: Exchanges a refresh token for new tokens (and, with rotation on, a new refresh token).

operations.name: tokens.password
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with their email and password in the database connection (the password-realm grant).

operations.name: tokens.emailCode
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with the one-time code Auth0 emailed them (the passwordless OTP grant).

operations.name: tokens.clientCredentials
operations.purpose: Gets a Management API token for the Machine to Machine application.

operations.name: tokens.revoke
operations.purpose: Revokes a refresh token, and the access tokens issued with it are no longer renewed.

operations.name: passwordless.start
operations.purpose: Emails a one-time sign-in code from the tenant's email connection.

operations.name: passwords.requestChange
operations.purpose: Emails a password reset link for a database connection user. Answers the same whether or not the address has an account.

operations.name: users.byEmail
operations.purpose: Lists the users with this email address, one per connection.

operations.name: users.create
operations.purpose: Creates a user in the database connection.

operations.name: users.update
operations.purpose: Updates a user: here, sets their password.

signature.description: Event streams sign nothing. A webhook stream with Bearer Token authentication sends Authorization: Bearer <token> with the token chosen when the stream was made; compare the whole header with 'Bearer ' + token in constant time. The body is a CloudEvent: id (evt_…), source, specversion, type, time, and data.object.

events.meaning: A user was created (signed up, or made through the Management API). data.object is the user.
A user's profile changed. data.object is the user.
A user was deleted. data.object is the user.
